items.text: A ring over a variable object
On a topos $B$ with an object $I$: build universally $B'\to B$ and a ring $A'$ over $I'$ (inverse image of $I$).
\{\text{ring on }I'\}=\{I'\to R\}=\{I'\to R\times B\},\quad R=\text{classifying topos of rings}
R_B:=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Top}_B}(I,\,R\times B)
Existence is clear: an algebraic theory plus one more object $A$ hidden in the pocket, then arrows $A\times_I A\to A$ (multiplication, addition) and axioms.
I\ \text{constant of length }n\ :\quad \text{a ring over }\textstyle\coprod^n e=n\text{ rings},\quad\text{classifying topos }R^n\times B
General $I$: not seen how to describe it nicely.
SGA was needlessly heavy about inverse limits of topoi (fear of canonical isomorphisms); in general they are trivial.
A remark on the smoothness of the formalism
$C$ with finite inverse limits; $E$ with direct limits and finite inverse limits. Functors $C\to E$ $\leftrightarrow$ functors $\widehat C\to E$ commuting with direct limits;
F\colon C\to E\ \text{left exact}\iff \widehat F\colon\widehat C\to E\ \text{left exact}\qquad(E\text{ a topos})
Converse checked: if $E$ has a small strictly generating subcategory $C$ and the statement holds, then $E$ is a topos.
E\hookrightarrow\widehat C\ \text{fully faithful, with left adjoint }\widehat C\to E\text{ left exact}\ \Longrightarrow\ E\text{ topos}
Key for classifying topoi: built in a small number of steps; the axioms fit perfectly.
Contrast: enveloping abelian category of one object — transfinite construction, no visible objects.
Advice
Write the classifying topos of structures you know (abelian groups, schemes, local rings…) and study how they fit together; e.g. connected components of a classifying topos.
Classifying topoi of theories by finite inverse limits: connected, cohomologically acyclic.
Subgroup functor, compatible with inverse limits $=$ subgroups of the universal abelian group: abelian subsheaves of the universal abelian sheaf on the classifying topos for abelian groups.
Recapitulation asked of the room; declined for now.
General notion: categories with exactness conditions, functors preserving them: the category $\Delta$.
Elementary topoi (remark from the room)
Cartesian closed (function space right adjoint to the product) and a subobject classifier. Add finite limits; with small sums and a small generating family one recovers a topos.
\operatorname{Hom}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(X,Z^Y),\qquad \operatorname{Sub}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(X,\Omega)
Here we do not use internal $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}$: inverse image functors between topoi do not commute with it.
$G$ acting faithfully on $X$ is not an algebraic property (not stable under inverse image).
Topological spaces in a topos?
No reasonable notion found; Isbell has one for any category (duality: a space in groups = topological group).
Candidate: power-set object $P(X)$ with structure — does not commute with inverse images (only a canonical arrow).
Infinite intersections do not commute with inverse limits of the kind used here.
Topoi without points
Structures given by topoi are not determined by their set-theoretic realisations; $T(\mathbf{Ens})$ may be empty although the topos is non-trivial.
\text{Deligne’s example: }[0,1]\text{ with Lebesgue measure; site = measurable sets mod null sets}
Coverings: countable subfamilies whose union is everything up to a null set. No points, yet a big topos.
Algebraic theories in the seminar’s sense: built stepwise; in topoi arbitrary direct limits and finite inverse limits are allowed (e.g. torsors).
Classifying topos for fields
Site: reduced schemes of finite type over $\mathbb Z$; closed immersions that are bijective inverted (kill nilpotents); decomposition into open $+$ closed complement is a covering.
To a scheme $X$ associate $X_{\mathrm{cons}}$: opens = unions of constructible sets; closed = intersections of constructible sets. Same points, locally compact; stalks the residue fields.
Affine $X$: decompose into $n$ locally closed constructible pieces (reduced structure); product of $n$ rings of functions.
\mathcal C(X)=\varinjlim_{\text{decompositions}}\ \prod_{i=1}^n \mathcal O(X_i)\quad\text{(constructible functions)}
\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal C(X)=\varprojlim\ \textstyle\coprod_{i=1}^n X_i\ \text{(compact, same points as }X)
Category: these compact schemes with constructible maps. Sheaves: contravariant functors to sets turning sums into products.
Universal ring: $X\mapsto$ ring of constructible functions. Absolutely flat rings (every module flat; reduced, compact spectrum), with a finiteness condition over $\mathbb Z$.
Likewise: universal algebraically closed field, normal ring, connected ring… (the notes give many).
Flat modules over a ring in a topos
Known criterion (compatible with inverse images, Deligne): for every finitely generated ideal $J\subset A$,
M\otimes_A J\longrightarrow M\ \text{ injective}
Over each object $U$: $J=\sum_{i=1}^n f_iA_U$, $f_i\in A(U)$.
Universal system of $n$ sections: $U_n=A^n$; $A_{U_n}=A^{n+1}$ over $U_n$; projections $f_1,\dots,f_n$.
J_n=\textstyle\sum_{i}f_iA_{U_n},\qquad M_{U_n}\otimes J_n\to M_{U_n}\ \text{monomorphism, for every }n
Universal case suffices: ideals, tensor products and monomorphisms are compatible with inverse images.
So flatness = a countable family of axioms (arrows made invertible). Equivalence with exactness of $\otimes$ in a topos: not checked.
